name: Unraid-Home
description: Self-populating homepage for your Unraid server. Scans Docker for containers and shows each one as a tile with its WebUI link, icon and status. Edit mode (from your home network) lets you rename, regroup, pin and hide tiles, add links and pages, and pick themes. Optional: login with authenticator sign-in, alerts (ntfy, Gotify, Discord, webhook, email), uptime and update badges, server stats, and automation for Nginx Proxy Manager and Cloudflare Tunnel so your apps get internet addresses automatically. All settings are optional. Built entirely by AI (Claude, by Anthropic). Features are tested, but not every situation has been, so do your own due diligence before exposing it to the internet: keep the login on, use a strong password and 2FA, and review your Cloudflare, proxy and firewall settings. Use at your own risk.

paths.name: Docker socket
paths.description: Used to discover containers (and, only if you turn on Container controls, to start/stop/restart them). Note: the read-only flag does not limit what the Docker API allows.

paths.name: Unraid templates
paths.description: Optional. Lets the hover summaries use each app's Overview text from its Unraid template. Read-only; only the name, repository, overview and category are read.

paths.name: Config
paths.description: Stores your tile overrides and custom links

paths.name: Update status file
paths.description: Optional. Lets tiles show an Update badge for containers Unraid says are out of date. Read-only.

paths.name: Disk stats: array
paths.description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show array usage.

paths.name: Disk stats: cache
paths.description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show cache usage.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port the homepage is served on

variables.name: Page title
variables.description: Heading shown at the top of the page

variables.name: Server address
variables.description: Optional. IP or hostname used in app links. Leave blank to use whatever address you opened the homepage with.

variables.name: Show stopped containers
variables.description: Show stopped containers (dimmed)

variables.name: Only containers with a WebUI
variables.description: true = hide containers that have no WebUI set in their Unraid template

variables.name: Show Unraid link
variables.description: Add a tile for the Unraid dashboard itself

variables.name: Open in new tab
variables.description: Open apps in a new browser tab

variables.name: Read-only
variables.description: true = hide the Edit button and block changes

variables.name: Password
variables.description: Login password (12+ characters). Leave blank to have one generated on first start; it is printed once in this container's log and stored only as a salted hash.

variables.name: Remote domain
variables.description: Optional. Your main domain (e.g. example.com). Every app with a web UI then gets https://container-name.example.com as its Remote URL automatically. Can also be set on the page in Edit mode.

variables.name: Uptime checks
variables.description: Check that each app's Remote URL answers over the internet and show a status dot on its tile.

variables.name: Stats strip
variables.description: Show CPU, memory, disk and uptime at the top of the page.

variables.name: Alerts: ntfy URL
variables.description: Optional. Full ntfy topic address (e.g. https://ntfy.sh/my-secret-topic) for alerts.

variables.name: Alerts: Gotify URL
variables.description: Optional. Gotify server address. Also set the Gotify token.

variables.name: Alerts: Gotify token
variables.description: Optional. Gotify app token.

variables.name: Alerts: Discord webhook
variables.description: Optional. Discord webhook address for alerts.

variables.name: Alerts: generic webhook
variables.description: Optional. Any address that accepts a JSON POST.

variables.name: Email: SMTP server
variables.description: Optional. Mail server for email alerts, e.g. smtp.gmail.com (Gmail needs an app password)

variables.name: Email: port
variables.description: Optional. 587 (STARTTLS, default), 465 (TLS) or 25 (plain relay)

variables.name: Email: user
variables.description: Optional. SMTP login (usually your email address)

variables.name: Email: password
variables.description: Optional. SMTP password. Gmail (and most providers with 2-step verification) require an app-specific password, not your normal password. Create a Gmail one at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords (2-Step Verification must be on first).

variables.name: Email: from
variables.description: Optional. Sender address (defaults to the SMTP user)

variables.name: Email: to
variables.description: Optional. Who gets alerts; comma-separated addresses

variables.name: NPM address
variables.description: Optional. Nginx Proxy Manager admin address, e.g. http://192.168.xxx.xxx:7818. Lets Edit mode create proxy hosts for your apps.

variables.name: NPM user
variables.description: Optional. An Nginx Proxy Manager user (email) with permission to manage Proxy Hosts. Use a separate user without two-factor login.

variables.name: NPM password
variables.description: Optional. That user's password.

variables.name: NPM forward address
variables.description: Optional. Address Nginx Proxy Manager should forward to (your Unraid IP). Blank = the host in NPM address.

variables.name: NPM automatic sync
variables.description: true = every few minutes, create proxy hosts for new apps automatically (never edits or deletes existing ones).

variables.name: Cloudflare API token
variables.description: Optional. Token limited to this zone's DNS edit and the account's Tunnel edit (and Access edit if you use it). See the README.

variables.name: Cloudflare account ID
variables.description: Optional. Your Cloudflare account ID.

variables.name: Cloudflare tunnel ID
variables.description: Optional. The ID of your Cloudflare Tunnel.

variables.name: Cloudflare Access emails
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated emails allowed through a Cloudflare Access login for the whole wildcard. Leave blank to skip Access.

variables.name: Remote edits blocked
variables.description: true = editing is only possible from your home network, not through a tunnel or reverse proxy

variables.name: Allowed countries
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated 2-letter country codes (e.g. US,CA). Only these can reach the page from the internet. Needs Cloudflare (it supplies the country).

variables.name: Blocked countries
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated country codes to refuse (e.g. CN,RU). Ignored if Allowed countries is set.

variables.name: Allowed host names
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated host names the page may be opened by (e.g. home.example.com,192.168.1.10). Anything else is refused.

variables.name: Login-free networks
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated addresses/CIDRs on your LAN that skip the login (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24). Never applies to tunnel/proxy traffic.

variables.name: Login required
variables.description: Turn the login off only if something else in front already protects the page

variables.name: Container controls
variables.description: true = show start / stop / restart buttons on tiles when you are on your home network. Needs Docker API write access (a socket proxy must allow POST and start/stop/restart). Off by default.
